claim: The Codeberg source is Kangel/Plugins-Store on default branch main at commit 3a9417b85597127d843b0411792721f111297a0a; repository metadata reports mirror=false.
recipe: Pin source analysis to this repository and commit; do not infer content parity from the word mirror.

claim: The repository README describes its files as plugins for Kangel Plugins Manager; it gives no developer SDK guide.
recipe: Use the catalog and packaged manager as references; consult the client SDK source separately for authoring contracts.

claim: The root LICENSE is GNU General Public License version 3, dated 29 June 2007.
recipe: Check the repository license before reusing catalog or manager files.

claim: The catalog snapshot has 700 plugin IDs; every record has url, name, version, author, status, hash, and signature fields.
api: store.json object keyed by plugin ID
recipe: Read the record by its top-level plugin ID; treat optional version-compatibility and dependency fields as per-entry metadata.

claim: Catalog download URLs point to Codeberg raw files on branch main and therefore move when that branch changes.
recipe: For reproducible downloads, record the catalog commit and verify downloaded bytes against the entry hash and signature.

claim: Against GitHub snapshot 513e29a07858e5dec3a8dcdc6a860fe4296f1d43, Codeberg has two extra IDs, custom_gifts and spam_collapse. Of 698 common records, 257 differ in legacy_version after excluding only the top-level url; 255 of those differences disappear when nested URLs are also excluded, so they are URL rewrites rather than legacy metadata drift.
recipe: Compare mirror catalogs after removing URL fields recursively before treating metadata as divergent; preserve mirror-specific URLs separately.

claim: After excluding URL fields recursively, 696 of 698 common records match; plugin_guard and camera_enhancer differ in current version, hash, and signature, and camera_enhancer also differs in min_version. Their legacy_version entries also contain substantive hash/signature differences.
recipe: Compare signatures, hashes, compatibility fields, and legacy entries as well as plugin IDs, while normalizing all mirror-specific URLs.

claim: The mirror workflow runs on pushes to main or manual dispatch, rewrites host-specific raw URLs, then pushes to GitHub, Codeberg, and GitVerse.
recipe: Treat workflow source as the intended mirror policy; inspect remote heads separately to establish actual synchronization.

claim: The bundled KPM package is ID kangel_plugins_manager version 1.5.4, declares app_version >=12.9.0 and sdk_version >=1.4.5.3, and marks itself compiled=false.
recipe: Use these as requirements declared by this KPM package, not a compatibility guarantee for other client releases.

claim: The manager archive build config declares zipFormat eaf and source kpmplugin/src; its stats report 91 uncompiled builds and zero compiled or failed builds.
recipe: Inspect both metainfo and builder stats; the package build number does not by itself prove a compiled artifact.

claim: The bundled Store supports Codeberg catalog URL https://codeberg.org/Kangel/Plugins-Store/raw/branch/main/store.json and checks latest commit using the Codeberg Forgejo commits API.
recipe: Select the Codeberg mirror mode to use this endpoint pair; auto mode may choose an earlier mirror first.

claim: In auto mode KPM probes mirrors in order Kangel, GitHub, Codeberg, GitVerse; after a successful refresh it stores the normalized catalog, commit SHA, and timestamp in .kpm_cache.json only when the mirror SHA request succeeds.
recipe: Use forced refresh when the caller needs to bypass a matching cached SHA; account for mirror-specific SHAs and links.

claim: Store data accepts either a URL string or a metadata object and normalizes compatibility, dependencies, requirements, hashes, signatures, status, localized descriptions, and legacy versions.
recipe: Preserve unknown optional catalog fields when extending readers; normalize requirements to a list before consuming them.

claim: KPM's normal install path blocks data that fails its hash/signature check when block_untrusted_plugins is enabled; that setting defaults to true at this call site.
recipe: For normal store installs, retain the trust gate before writing a .py or extracting an .eaf; this observation covers only this KPM version.

claim: Signature verification uses Java SHA256withRSA over the UTF-8 message plugin_id:version:file_hash and a public key loaded from the package asset public_key.pem.
recipe: Match the ID, version, and lowercase or uppercase-insensitive SHA-256 value before verifying a catalog signature.

claim: The selected-plugin update path checks client compatibility and compares local and remote version strings, then writes changed content without calling _check_plugin_data in that method.
recipe: When reviewing this KPM version, assess update integrity separately from the normal install gate; this static observation is not a runtime exploit finding.

claim: KPM registers its menu and hooks from on_plugin_load; on_plugin_unload removes tracked hooks and menu items and clears badge/cache state.
recipe: Track registered hooks and UI resources so unload can release them; these are manager implementation patterns, not proof of public SDK API.

claim: The deeplink hook handles tg://kpm_install, tg://kpm_list, and FAQ routes from LaunchActivity.handleIntent and moves install or refresh work onto run_on_queue.
recipe: Parse a deep link only after matching its route prefix and hand download work off the intent/UI hook thread.

claim: Repository documentation describes a plain .plugin as one Python file and Elyx .eaf/.elyx as a ZIP with a root refmap pointing to metainfo, main, strings, and assets; metadata filename variants and archive fallback lookup are also documented.
recipe: Treat these as the repository author's format conventions; verify a specific package and consult the SDK for normative client contracts.

claim: AGENTS.md documents hash as SHA-256 over the plugin file bytes and gives a Python hashlib.sha256(open(path, 'rb').read()).hexdigest() example.
recipe: Hash the exact binary artifact bytes; a matching catalog string alone does not verify a downloaded artifact.

claim: For legacy_versions, the repository instructions say to archive old releases under versioned names without overwriting an existing file; if the same name exists with a different hash, append a numeric collision suffix such as _1.
recipe: Preserve an existing legacy artifact on filename collision and choose a new numeric suffix when hashes differ.
